where: Figure, caption and the 'Material D_m' node note
problem: The figure note says the material part has 'zero ≈ 1310 nm' and the caption says the material zero 'is fixed near 1310 nm by the glass'. This contradicts the text, which puts the material zero near 1300 nm and the fiber zero near 1310 nm. 1310 nm is where D_m + D_w = 0, not where D_m = 0. A student reading only the figure will conclude the glass itself has zero material dispersion at 1310 nm.
fix: Change the node note to 'zero ≈ 1300 nm (silica)' and the caption to: '... a material part, whose zero is fixed near 1300 nm by the glass, and a waveguide part, which a designer moves by changing the profile; the two add with their signs to put the fiber zero near 1310 nm.'

problem: The answer says D_m at 1310 nm is 'about +3 ps/(nm·km)', which implies the material zero sits near 1275 nm. The text says the material zero is near 1300 nm, and with the stated slope of about 0.09 ps/(nm²·km) a 10 nm offset gives only about +1 ps/(nm·km). The two statements do not agree.
fix: Either write D_m ≈ +1 ps/(nm·km) at 1310 nm, or state in Section 2 that the silica material zero is nearer 1275-1280 nm and keep +3 in Q7. Use one figure in both places.

problem: 'That spreading is chromatic dispersion, quoted in ps/(nm·km)' mixes the spread (a time, in ps) with the coefficient (ps/(nm·km)). A student may quote the pulse spread in ps/(nm·km).
fix: Write: 'That spreading is chromatic dispersion; the spread Δτ is in ps, and the fiber is described by a dispersion coefficient D in ps/(nm·km).'

problem: 'Some call the red-first case positive' uses 'red-first' without definition; many readers will not connect red with the longer wavelength.
fix: Write: 'Some books take D positive when the longer wavelength arrives first; this book takes it positive when the longer wavelength arrives later.'
